chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and Husayn ibn Uthman, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who died and some of his heirs acknowledged a debt on his behalf to a man, he (the Imam) said: 'That debt binds him in his share.' This does not contradict the first two narrations, because his saying 'That debt binds him in his share' is to be understood as binding him to the extent of what he receives (his portion of the estate), not that the entire debt binds him. This is indicated by the first two detailed narrations. And this narration is general (mujmal), and it should be interpreted according to the detailed ones, as we have explained in other places.

key_terms.إِقْرَار: Acknowledgment or confession of a debt

ai.seo_question: How is a debt distributed among heirs when only some acknowledge it on behalf of the deceased?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to resolve apparent contradictions in fiqh by interpreting the heir's liability as proportional to their specific share of the estate rather than joint and several. This principle ensures that an heir who acknowledges a debt is not unfairly burdened with the entire amount, aligning with the broader Shia legal methodology of reconciling *mujmal* (general) and *mufassal* (detailed) texts. It highlights the precision of Imami jurisprudence in distinguishing between personal acknowledgment and collective estate obligation.
